blocks.text: Setting up your IT hub in Notion

As an IT coordinator, you need a single source of truth. Your Notion workspace should host your infrastructure maps, configuration guides, and onboarding checklists. Start by creating a top-level page for your IT department. Use a database to store your hardware inventory. Include properties for serial numbers, purchase dates, and current status. You can filter these views by location or device type to find what you need quickly.

Efficiency matters when you are juggling support tickets. Type / to open the block menu in any Notion page. This lets you add headers, tables, or checkboxes without leaving your keyboard. For example, type /table to create a new database. Type /callout to highlight important safety warnings in your runbooks. These shortcuts save time during your busy day on macOS.

Documentation often becomes outdated. Set up a review system using a date property in your database. Create a view that shows documents modified more than six months ago. This prompts you to verify if the steps are still accurate. Use toggles to hide complex details in your guides. This keeps the page readable for end-users while keeping the technical depth available for your team.

blocks.text: Do not over-engineer your databases early on. Start with simple tables and add properties only when you need them. Avoid creating too many sub-pages. It makes navigation difficult. Stick to a clear hierarchy. Ensure your permissions are set correctly from the start. Limit edit access to sensitive configuration pages to prevent accidental changes.
If you are unsure where a specific setting is located in the Notion menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur. It will point to the menu item or the button on your screen.
blocks.title: Find settings faster

blocks.text: Your Mac is your primary tool. Use ⌘ Space to launch apps quickly. Keep your Notion desktop app updated via the Notion menu. If you encounter issues, use ⌘ R to reload the page. This often fixes sync errors. Ensure your macOS version is 13 or higher for the best performance.

Lazur helps you handle the repetitive parts of your job. When you are writing a new runbook, hold fn to dictate your notes directly into Notion. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the screen. If you are struggling with a complex formula, ask Lazur to explain how it works. It can clarify the logic without you having to search through documentation.

Use relations to connect your projects to your tasks. This gives you a clear view of how your daily work contributes to larger infrastructure goals. Use rollups to aggregate data from related databases. For example, you can see the total cost of hardware associated with a specific project. This is helpful when reporting to management.

faq.question: Can I use Notion offline on Mac?
faq.answer: Notion requires an internet connection for most features. You can view cached pages, but editing is limited without a connection.

faq.question: How do I move a page in Notion?
faq.answer: Click and hold the six-dot icon next to the block. Drag it to the new location in the sidebar or on the page.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Notion?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can use it to dictate text, search, or get help with interface elements.
